Senator Michael Tipping, Senate Chair

Bill Brown, Director of Actuarial and Legislative Affairs
LD 1021, An Act to Remove Certain Cost-of-living Adjustment Restrictions for
Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Who Are 65 Years of
Age or Older

Good morning Senator Tipping, Chair Roeder and the other distinguished members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Labor. I am Bill Brown, Director of Actuarial and Legislative Affairs for
the Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MainePERS).
MainePERS is neither for nor against LD 1021. We are here to provide information and to offer
any assistance the committee may request surrounding this bill.
State employee and teacher pensions receive cost of living adjustments (COLAs) tied to the
Consumer Price lndex (CPI). The current cap ("COLA cap") on COLA is 3%, established in 2011. Also in 2011 the amount of a retiree's benefits on which the COLA applies ("COLA Base") was limited to $20,000, indexed annually based on the percentage of COLA paid. The 2025 COLA base is $26,428.98. A sheet detailing the most recent history of COLA changes is
attached to this testimony.
It is our understanding after speaking with those familiar with the bill that the intent is to remove
the COLA Base once a retiree from one of the stated positions reaches age 65, effective with the COLA awarded in September 2025.As drafted, the bill appears to require coverage for
employees who retire at age 65 or older,. However, the majority of the positions covered are
currently included in special plans that permit retirement well before age 65. Specifically, the
COLA base for current retirees who are at least age 65 would be removed and those who are not yet age 65 as well as future retirees would have no COLA base limitation when they reach
~
age 65. If that is the intent, we are happy to work with the bill sponsor and the Committee Analyst to amend the bill to ensure the intent is clear.
This bill will have a fiscal impact as the Maine Constitution does not permit the creation of new or additional benefits unless they are immediately and fully funded. LD 1021 creates additional benefits that are not currently accounted for or funded, creating a new unfunded actuarial liability (UAL). UAL and normal costs attributable to this proposed change remain to be
calculated. We have not yet obtained costs for this bill pending guidance from the Committee.
Thank you for your consideration of this testimony. l am happy to answer questions and we will
be present for the work session.

Testimony of Senator Craig I/. Hickman in support of
LD 1021, "An Act to Remove Certain Cost-of-living Adjustment Restrictions for Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Who Are 65 Years of Age or Older,"
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Labor Wednesday, March 26
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder, and honorable members of the Committee on Labor, my name is Craig Hickman and I am proud to represent Senate District 14, twelve municipalities in southern Kennebec County including my beloved hometown of Winthrop. Thank you for the opportunity to speak in support of LD 1021, "An Act to Remove Certain Cost-of-living Adjustment Restrictions for Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Who Are 65 Years of
Age or Older."
As many of you are aware, I am and have long been a strong supporter of Maine law enforcement
and an active proponent of giving our public service retirees what they were promised.
Before 2011, members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit were promised full COLAs when they retired. However, in 2011, that was reduced: COLAs were only applied to part of their pensions.
I see this as a broken promise.
Our law enforcement officers do so much for our communities and sacrifice so much in the process.
They deserve to be fairly compensated for this work, and they have earned a dignified retirement. This bill helps ensure that retirement is as dignified as possible by providing cost of living adjustments for their full retirement benefit. Our retired law enforcement officers must be able to keep up with rising costs, just like the rest of us.
We must show them, with our actions and with our treasure, how grateful We are for their service. We
must ensure past promises are kept.
Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to speak in support of this bill.
I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.
Craig V. Hickman

My name is Kevin Anderson, and I am the Executive Director of the Maine State Law Enforcement Association. I am here to testify in support of LD 1021 on behalf of the Maine Law
Enforcement Coalition. The Maine Law Enforcement Coalition collectively represents over 95% of Maine Law Enforcement Officers in the State of Maine. The members of the coalition include the Maine State Law Enforcement Association, the Maine State Law Enforcement Supervisors
Association, the Maine State Troopers Association and the Maine Association of Police.
LD 1021 is the result of hours of work conducted by Retired AG Detective Mike Pulire in a
partnership with Representative Brenner and supported strongly by others to include Senator
Hickman who you have heard from or will here from in support of this bill today.
The intent of this bill is to remove the COLA cap on retirees over the age of 65 who have given
their life to public service in the law enforcement field. These men and women gave their minds
and bodies during some of their best years of there lives to protect Maine's citizens and those
that visit this amazing state. These brave men and women deserve recognition for their sacrifices.
A small token of this recognition would be to support the removal of the COLA cap from the
retirement benefits of those officers who are 65 years of age and older.

This bill only afiects coalition members that retire as state law enforcement officers as our
municipal and county law enforcement partners who retire from PLD plans do not feel the sting of restricted COLA's upon retirement like the retired state law enforcement officers do.

Current research indicates that law enforcement officers on average live 10-21 years shorter lives
than those that have not served in the law enforcement career field. A sobering number and one
worthy of consideration when this committee considers this bill in the days in weeks to come.

served, are serving, or are considering serving, by voting ought to pass on LD 1021.

that you may have at this time.

Michael Pulire, Detective, Maine Attorney General (Ret.)
Founding Member, First President, Maine State Law Enforcement Association (Ret.)
March 26, 2025
My name is Michael Pulire and l sit before you today in support of LD 1021 an Act
to Remove Certain Cost-of-Living Adjustment Restrictions for Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Age 65 and Oder. The Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit (LEBU) is composed of sworn state
officers' servings as: Game Wardens, Marine Patrol Officers, Fire Marshal Investigators, Probation Officers (Adult & Juvenile), Secretary of State Detectives,
Baxter State Park Rangers, Capital Police Officers, DOC Detectives, Forest
Rangers, Military Police Officers, Judicial Marshals and Attorney General Detectives. Thirteen groups of state law enforcement missions.
I was first sworn as a Maine cop in 1975 serving as a Reserve in Ogunquit while attending college. I was hired full time in 1976 by the City of Gardiner and
graduated from the MCJA 29"` Basic School in March of 1978. By the end of the
year, I left the profession for reasons addressed in the attrition findings of the Law Enforcement Stakeholder's Group report to the Legislature submitted this month. I spent the next decade conducting investigations for the insurance industry until I was recruited back to public service in 1989 and commissioned as a detective
with the Office of Attorney General. I served in that capacity for 33 years until my
retirement in good standing on the last day of August 2022.
"Retirement" , is a noun. Oxford, Cambridge and Wikipedia all have common themes in their definitions such as "ceasing to work" and "too old" as well as
the end of "active working life" . Retirement benefits are part of a contract; in this case, between the state and
those who served in public safety roles. What joined contractual party gets to
unilaterally alter the provisions of a contract to the detriment of others with no negotiation, due process or recourse for those injured parties to the contract?
My generation of state LEOs have been subject to changes in vesting and retirement age requirements over our state careers. In my particular case, the AG Detectives did not receive a special law enforcement retirement plan until just
the last few years. I in fact retired in a standard 25-year age 62 plan.
Since 2011 with COLAs for state retirees restricted to one size fits all the state
has enjoyed only small, easy to calculate fiscal notes for this contractual
obligation hitting very hard the professional classes of state employees who earn far more in retirement compensation than $20K, now $26K after 14 years. Many
in this class were required to hold state/federal Iicensure to practice their

training, expertise or legal authority to conduct these specialty operations. 10.At age 65+ what parttime employment opportunities are there to practice our
vocation'? In most every case, there is none based simply on the passage of time.
lt is a rare individual who at that age can compete for positions and then engage
in the nature of that work.
11.The age 65+ retired members of the LEBU fare no better in qualifying as a reserve officer with a municipal police agency, again, given the demands of such
service. Potential earnings in that venue range from $28-$38 an hour. A far cry

full COLA adds another $800.00 to that average retirement.

most cases involving death. In that time, I may have logged a hall million miles

Testimony of Senator Stacy Brenner in support of LD 1021, "An Act to Remove Certain Cost-oil living Adjustment Restrictions for Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Who
Are 65 Years of Age or Older" Before the Joint Standing Committee on Labor
March 26, 2025
Representative Roeder, Senator Tipping and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Labor. I am Senator Stacy Brenner, representing Senate District 30 which includes all of Gorham and
most of Scarborough. I am before you today to present LD 1021, An Act to Remove Certain Cost-ojiliving
Adjustments Restrictions for Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Who Are 65 Years ofAge or Older.
This bill is quite straightforward, it will allow retired members of law enforcement and those part of their bargaining unit to receive cost of living adjustments (COLAs) and remove the restrictions that are currently in place. By lifiing these restrictions, this bill seeks to bring due justice to our retirement system,
ensuring those who have spent their careers serving and protecting Mainer's are not left behind.
From Marine Patrolers to Game Wardens to Correction Officers, Maine's law enforcement officers
dedicate their lives and careers to protecting public safety, often in demanding and dangerous conditions.
This is why it is important to support these individuals as they enter retirement and ensure they receive the compensation they rightfully have earned. In fact, retired members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit aged 65 years or older were offered full COLAs from the state until 2011 when the chief
executive at the time reversed this policy with no due process for the affected population of vested
employees. These COLA restrictions have placed undue financial strain on many retired officers, making
it harder for them to keep up with the rising costs of everyday expenses.
Today's legislation does away with this by removing these restrictions on COLAs so that retired law
enforcement officers can be able to receive pensions that are sustainable and can meet the reality of fluctuating expenses such as energy costs and food costs. This legislation is vital to offset inflation and to
preserve the purchasing power of retirees' income who have paid into these pensions.
I'd also like to introduce an amendment to this legislation to read "all state retired law enforcement
officers age 65 and older" . This change will allow LD 1021 to cover all retirees from the Maine State Law
Enforcement Association, Maine State Trooper Association and the Maine State Law Enforcement
Supervisory Bargaining Unit. This addition will ensure all line officers and field supervisors that
represent state law enforcement will receive these COLAs. l'd like to note that representatives from these
additional groups will be reaching out to Kathy Morin at MePERS to request a determination of how
many retirees that are age 65 and older that are collecting a state pension. I hope to have this data for you by the work session.
The best of us choose to serve and protect us, I ask now that the best of us serve and protect them. I urge
you all to support LD 1021. Thank you.

SUBJECT: LD 1021, An Act to Remove Certain Cost-of-Living Adjustment Restrictions for Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Who Are 65 Years of Age or Older

Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Labor. My
name is William H. Laubenstein, III. I am President of the Maine Association of Retirees (MAR) whose
membership includes retired State employees, retired teachers and other public service retirees.
MAR is neither for nor against LD 2021, which, beginning in 2025, would require the Board of Directors
of Maine Public Employee Retirement System (MainePERS) to apply the cost-of-living (COLA)
percentage increase in retirement benefits up to the maximum annual increase of 3% to the full pension benefit of certain law enforcement officers age 65 or older. Applying the COLA to the full-service
retirement benefit for this select group of retirees inequitably distinguishes this group from retired State
and teacher retirees whose benefit is limited to 3% of an indexed amount which in 2024 was $26,659.20.
While MAR applauds any effort to address the severe impact of changes to the calculation of the COLA in 2011, as a matter of policy and equity, MAR does not support bifurcating or otherwise drawing distinctions
between one set or class of retirees and all other retirees. Allowing a distinction between one group of retirees and other retirees is a sloppy slope, inviting others to advocate for their favorite group. Retired State employees
and teachers as well law enforcement officers age 65 and older and other public service retirees suffered when
in 2011 the COLA was changed from a maximum annual increase of 4% on a retirees' full pension to a maximum annual increase of 3% on an indexed amount.`
MAR welcomes Senator Brenner to the chorus of legislators who are seeking ways to alleviate the hardship
experienced by retirees as a result of rising inflation that continues to erode their already limited purchasing
power.
Nevertheless, MAR is committed to adhering to its policy of advocating for all retirees as a matter of equity
and fairness.
